title: Linear Search
question: What is the time complexity of this search?
explanation: We iterate through every element once in the worst case — exactly n comparisons, so O(n).

title: Array Index Access
code: int value = arr[42];
question: What is the time complexity of this operation?
explanation: Direct index access in an array uses a base address + offset calculation — always one step regardless of array size.

title: Bubble Sort
question: What is the worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Two nested loops each running up to n times gives n × n = n² comparisons in the worst case.

title: Binary Search
question: What is the time complexity of this search?
explanation: Each iteration halves the search space — after k steps we have n/2^k elements left. Solving 2^k = n gives k = log₂n.

title: Merge Sort
question: What is the average-case time complexity?
explanation: The array is split log n times (depth of recursion tree) and each level does O(n) work during merge — giving n log n total.

title: Hash Map Lookup
question: What is the average-case time complexity for each operation?
explanation: Hash maps compute a hash of the key and jump directly to that bucket — O(1) average for both insert and lookup (assuming few collisions).

title: Recursive Fibonacci
question: What is the time complexity of this naive implementation?
explanation: Each call branches into two sub-calls. The recursion tree has depth n, giving approximately 2^n total nodes — exponential growth.

title: Quicksort
question: What is the average-case time complexity?
explanation: On average, partition splits evenly — log n recursive levels × O(n) partitioning = O(n log n). Worst case (sorted input, bad pivot) is O(n²).

title: All Subsets
question: What is the time complexity of generating all subsets?
explanation: Each element has two choices — include or exclude. For n elements, there are 2^n possible subsets, so the algorithm must visit 2^n nodes.

title: All Permutations
question: What is the time complexity of generating all permutations?
explanation: There are n! permutations of n elements. The recursion tree has n levels and branches n, n-1, n-2… times — total nodes is n × (n-1) × … × 1 = n!.

title: Triplet Sum
question: What is the time complexity of this triple-loop?
explanation: Three nested loops each iterating up to n times results in O(n³) comparisons — cubic time.

title: BFS Traversal
question: What is the time complexity of BFS on an adjacency list?
explanation: Each vertex is enqueued once (O(V)) and each edge is explored once (O(E)) — total is O(V + E).

title: Heap Sort
question: What is the time complexity of heap sort?
explanation: Building the heap is O(n). Each of the n extract-max operations calls heapify at O(log n) — giving O(n) + O(n log n) = O(n log n).

title: Stack Push / Pop
question: What is the time complexity of push and pop operations?
explanation: Stack operations (push, pop, peek) only touch the top of the stack — they never iterate over elements, always O(1).

title: Matrix Chain Multiplication (DP)
question: What is the time complexity of this DP solution?
explanation: Three nested loops each of size O(n) — outer for chain length, middle for starting index, inner for split point — gives O(n³).

title: BST Insert
question: What is the average-case time complexity for BST insert?
explanation: In a balanced BST, the height is log n — each insert traverses at most one root-to-leaf path. Worst case (skewed tree) is O(n).

title: String Length
code: int len = strlen(s);  // C string (null-terminated)
question: What is the time complexity of strlen?
explanation: strlen must scan every character until it finds '\0' — it touches all n characters, so O(n). Note: std::string::size() is O(1).

title: Counting Sort
question: What is the time complexity of counting sort?
explanation: We iterate over n input elements once, then over k buckets once — total O(n + k). When k = O(n), this is O(n) — better than comparison sorts.

title: Power Function (Fast Exponentiation)
question: What is the time complexity of this exponentiation?
explanation: Each recursive call halves the exponent (even case) or reduces it by 1 then halves — the recursion depth is O(log exp).

title: Floyd-Warshall
question: What is the time complexity of Floyd-Warshall?
explanation: Three nested loops each running V times — one for intermediate vertex k, one for source i, one for destination j — gives exactly V³ iterations.
